text:
终于有人把“本地大模型打真实电话”做出来了，而且完全开源！

以往体验市面上的各类 AI 电话助手，最让人顾虑的就是隐私安全：通话录音、转写文本、沟通对象全都会留在第三方云端。开发者刚刚开源的 ai-phone 则彻底打通了本地闭环——让你的 Mac 直接接管真实电话线路，所有推理均在本地完成，通话数据完全不出机器。

🛠️ 核心技术栈（基于 Apple Silicon & MLX）：

语音识别（STT）： Parakeet TDT 0.6B 本地运行，极速语音转文字

语言模型（LLM）： 默认本地运行 Qwen3.5 4B（32GB 内存支持 9B 4-bit），同时也支持接入自己的 Claude 或 ChatGPT 端点

语音合成（TTS）： Kokoro 82M / Phonon，生成自然流畅的声音

通信接入： 通过 SIP 协议直连 Telnyx 或 Twilio，直接购买或绑定真实电话号码（月租约 1 美元）

✨ 核心亮点：

低延迟与实时打断： 在 Apple Silicon 芯片上实测首字响应延迟约 1~1.5 秒；支持实时插话打断（Interruption），一旦你开口，AI 会立刻停下倾听。

支持外部 Agent 联动： 提供了 call、listen、say、hangup 等标准化 CLI 接口，可以直接让 Claude Code、Codex 等编码智能体通过命令编排通话，自动完成预约餐厅、电话咨询等任务。

本地守护进程： 提供向导式 CLI 配置，一行命令拉起本地守护进程，静默接听来电或随时发起外呼。

⚠️ 当前要求与限制：

仅支持搭载 Apple Silicon 的 macOS 系统

目前为单路通话，优先支持英文环境

项目刚刚上线，对本地 AI 语音助手与 SIP 通信落地感兴趣的朋友值得关注：https://t.co/n2G7fQGsnG

1.风格引导：精准控制界面气质。支持一键放大视觉冲击力、弱化杂乱元素、修正字体排版与空间节奏，让千篇一律的 AI 设计迅速拥有独特的品牌辨识度。

text:
This is completely f*cking wild.

A Stanford AI researchers gave Claude Code a second brain with JEV. The result? 80+ billion data points processed every 14 minutes.

here's how it works:

Jev stands at the door. every row has to get past it first.

the easy ones it waves through on the spot. only the ones it can't call get sent upstairs to Claude.

the old way:
everything -> Claude -> big bill

the new way:
everything -> Jev -> the tricky few -> Claude

Jev also tells you how sure it is on every call. that number decides who goes upstairs. just don't pick it out of thin air. test it first.

the 20-minute setup:

1. take 200 real rows from your data
2. run them through Jev AND Claude
3. sort Jev's answers by how sure it was
4. find the point where Jev stops disagreeing with Claude. that's your cutoff
5. above it, Jev's answer is final. below it, the row goes to Claude

then do the math. on a public benchmark Jev cost $0.015 per 1,000 rows and Claude cost $0.80.

if Jev settles 80% of your rows:

$0.015 + (20% × $0.80) = $0.175 per 1,000 rows instead of $0.80

that's ~78% off, with Claude still handling every hard case.

3 rules that keep it working:

-> ask all your questions in one Jev call. topic, urgency and sentiment together, not three separate requests
-> once a week, send 50 of Jev's "confident" answers to Claude anyway. if they start disagreeing, raise the cutoff
-> never let Jev make the final call on anything you can't undo. refunds, bans, deletions go to Claude or a human

where this pays off right away:

-> support tickets: route by topic and urgency
-> leads: hot, warm or skip
-> comments: fine, spam or needs a look
-> spreadsheets: fix category labels across thousands of rows

Claude thinks. Jev picks. code ships.

[Cita @thegreatest_sv]: JEV: YOUR LLM’S SECOND BRAIN (Use Cases): Jev is not a chatbot. It's the cheap brain that decides - so your LLM can finally stop answering yes/no
Every agent you ship burns frontier tokens on stupid questions.
Is this email spam? Which worker

text:
Google Research publicó Harness²: un framework para que los agentes prueben y mejoren sus propias instrucciones, skills y herramientas.

frente a una tarea, el sistema:

1) propone cambios en cómo trabaja el agente.
2) ejecuta la misma tarea con distintas configuraciones.
3) compara cómo se comportó cada una y combina los ajustes para intentar mejorar su desempeño.
4) guarda las lecciones para orientar las próximas tareas.

el modelo sigue siendo el mismo. lo que cambia es todo lo que lo rodea y determina cómo trabaja: su harness.

> Escribe /schedule y dile "todas las mañanas a las 7:30, envíame lo que entró, lo que redactaste y lo que espera mi sí". De ahora en adelante trabaja en una rutina

text:
Google just open-sourced Harness².

(turn any harness into a self-improving system)

a harness is everything wrapped around the model, like the system prompt, tools, memory, skills, and subagents. today a person designs it once, and the agent runs every new task with that same fixed setup.

Harness² lets the agent refine that setup for each new task on its own, with the model weights left untouched.

on every task, the agent proposes edits to its harness, runs a few candidate versions, and composes a better harness by comparing how those runs behaved.

because it learns from the differences between runs, it needs no correct answer or grader for the task.

that covers a single task. Harness² also carries what it learns from one task into the next.

after each task, it saves the harness it settled on along with the lessons that held up across the runs. the next time it refines a harness, it starts from those notes instead of from scratch.

this means every finished task makes the next round of edits more informed.

Google tested this with Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 on legal, office, and professional work benchmarks. one round of edits was enough to beat their original harnesses, and giving the agent more rounds pushed scores higher.

those extra rounds can go wide or deep. the agent either tries several candidate harnesses at once or keeps refining a single one step by step, using OpenCode or Codex to carry out the work.

who the f*ck let a spider read my prompt... i am never writing one by hand again

i thought my prompt was clean, i had run it for weeks, then i let the spider read it like a stranger, 181 words, and the first score was 37 out of 100

→ every word tagged as a claim, an owner, a file, an approval or vague
→ the vague ones went into my second brain and came back with what i had already decided, 45 links
→ the 12 it could not resolve were flagged for me
→ 0 words guessed

final score 82, and i did not rewrite a single line.

the prompt was never bad, it was disconnected from everything i already knew, and now the spider pulls that context in so i stop typing it by hand.

text:
I STOPPED LETTING CLAUDE OPUS 5.5 MAKE DECISIONS THE DAY I BUILT THIS JEV AGENT FOLDER

I used to let Claude decide, write and act on every single step

-> now Claude only writes. Jev makes the calls, code does the acting, and every step leaves a receipt
10,000 decisions cost me $0.42

everything inside the folder:

• the input
> AGENTS.md - when to call Jev and when to skip it
> state/build_state - goal, workers, done, missing, constraint. evidence, never a summary

• Jev decides (questions/)
> route - which model tier gets the task
> next_worker - which worker moves next
> relevance - keep or drop every tool output
> done - is the goal really met
> risky - will this send, pay or delete something?

• code acts (rules/)
> hard_rules - stop after ten actions, never publish anything unapproved
> thresholds.yaml - act only on confident answers. fraud needs 0.95

• Claude writes (workers/)
> research - sources and notes
> writer - drafts and briefings
> the one place in the folder where text gets generated

• the proof
> receipts/decisions.jsonl - options offered, chosen id, re-check, fallback
> evals/ - dozens of my own labelled traces, thresholds tuned on them

• the guards (hooks/)
> pre_tool_use - every command checked before it runs
> stop - confirms "all done" before the agent is allowed to quit

median 300 ms per decision. the expensive model never waits on a yes or no again

the engineer who can show this bill to their team stops being the person who uses AI and becomes the one who decides how it runs

an LLM writes, Jev decides, code acts

text:
Stop writing Claude Code skills by hand. This tool writes them from your sessions.

It's called autoharness, a self-learning skill layer for Claude Code.

It watches the work you already do and turns it into skills. No separate data collection, no replay loop. It runs on its own once a session has done enough work, or you type /learn to save a lesson right away.

And it keeps the skill folder clean:

→ Merges skills that cover the same scenario instead of adding another near-copy
→ Updates skills while they're being used
→ Archives the ones that stop getting used
→ Only touches the skills it wrote. Yours are never modified

Why this matters: with the same model, a better harness took CORE-Bench from 42% to 78%. The harness does much of the work, but people still rebuild it by hand for every new model. autoharness bets the skill part can maintain itself.

Two commands to install inside Claude Code. Pure Python, no dependencies.

100% open source. MIT.

text:
Jev + GPT-6 Astra just won 9 out of 10 StarCraft II games

Astra made the plan. Jev picked the next move while the game kept running

The team tested five setups across 50 matches against the game's toughest built-in opponent without cheats:

> Jev alone → 0/10 wins
> Astra's plan + random moves → 0/10
> Astra's plan + Jev's moves → 9/10

A good plan wasn't enough. The moves had to keep up with it

Across the tests, Jev returned 19,605 decisions and Astra replied 509 times. In the 9/10 setup, Jev's median response took 0.375 seconds

In a separate test of 210 smaller battles, Jev alone eliminated 16.50% of enemy forces on average. Jev + Astra reached 37.69% - about 2.3x as much

In an earlier set of four wins, estimated model usage averaged $3.71 per game: $0.15 for Jev and $3.56 for Astra

The loop is simple:

> Astra plans ahead
> Jev picks an available move
> the game plays it
> both get the new state

Those 9 wins came from the whole setup: the plan, the available moves and the fast choices between them

動画編集、Premiere Proもカット作業の外注もいらない時代が来ました。

Claude Codeに素材を投げるだけで、
完全自動でプロ品質の動画が仕上がる『video-use』が登場。

👇

やっていることはかなりシンプルで、

まず用意するのは撮影した動画素材（フォルダに入れるだけ）。
次に用意するのがClaude Code。

この2つを繋いで「ローンチ動画にして」とチャットするだけで、勝手に完パケ動画が書き出される。

・無音＆フィラー（えー、あのー）の完全自動カット
・色味の自動シネマティック補正
・音ズレやつなぎ目の音声ノイズ完全除去
・単語単位の字幕テロップ生成
・書き出しミスをAI自らプレビュー検品して自動リテイク

ポイントは
「AIに動画丸ごと見せてトークンを溶かす」のではなく、
音声文字起こし＋必要な瞬間だけ波形・コマを確認する超高効率アーキテクチャなこと。

これまでなら、動画編集者に数万円払って
3〜5日待って修正依頼を投げていた作業が、
ターミナル上で数分で完成するのバグすぎw

しかも100%オープンソースです。

「まだ動画編集は人間がカチカチやるもの」と思っている人ほど、この差はどんどん開いていきます。

今いちばん手に入れておくべきAIエージェントスキルが、ここにある。

リプ欄にGitHubの導入コマンド貼っておきます👇

ざっくり言うと、こんなモデルです。
